This movie is about rich people and their good habits !! The thing is, this movie falls at every level and I mean every single level except camerawork and cinematography and that piano score because these are the only things done by Mr. Stanley Kubrick in this movie other than that he just used his name after him. The movie tries to be toxic relationships type but doesn't work in that then it tries to create some mystery around some secret society and all and that also doesn't work not even one time. Tom Cruise is phenomenal but only in his looks, acting-wise he is just decent but Nicole Kidman is really phenomenal in both looks as well as in acting. The screenplay feels completely lost and confused in itself and the characters feel very random just like thrown in the story. The psychological thing about relationships and marriage and guilt and making other people feel guilty out of nowhere feels completely trash and the secret society thing didn't even touch in the movie except that 10 min scene, no front or back story nothing, the whole movie is just Tom Cruise walking on the streets. The most strange thing is, we saw the whole story through the perspective of Tom Cruise's character but why there is no narration and because of it the movie feels so empty and blank at many times. I completely agree with the theory that this cut is not the original cut of the movie by Stanley Kubrick.

"Nenhum sonho é apenas um sonho" Me irritei muito com aquela expressão na cara do Bill o tempo todo,ele sempre fazia aquele "quase sorriso" toda vez que começava a falar e quando terminava. Além de arranjar  um pretexto para ******* com outras mulheres só por causa de um sonho sexual que a Alice contou envolvendo ela mesma. Tudo bem que ela poderia ter esse desejo sexual,ela deixou bem claro pra ele durante a conversa,mas aquilo ao meu ver não foi uma traição porque ela contou a ele como se sentia...e tudo aquilo não foi real,no final das contas. E ele tinha uma descrição bem vivida da esposa dele com apenas um cara,mesmo que ela tenha contado que também se envolveu com outros,mas ela teve uma atração real só por um,ela só seria capaz de abandonar tudo só por aquele cara em específico. E ele não pensava na própria traição, ele tava mais incomodado com a traição da esposa. Alice estava tendo esses sonhos sexuais e ela se sentiu culpada depois,mas enquanto tinha os sonhos,ela ria com a possibilidade do Bill poder ver o que ela estava fazendo. Por que eles ainda decidiram ficar juntos? não pra sempre,porque a ideia assustava Alice. Ela simplesmente disse que eles deveriam estar agradecidos por estarem acordados. Eu tava esperando que no final,Alice respondesse que o que eles deveriam fazer era  se divorciarem,mas é muito realista,então vamos ficar no imaginário sexual mesmo.

Man, the writing is wretched in some scenes. It’s laughably bad. It gets much better in the second half but the first half was Razzie worthy. Cruise and Kidman both take opportunities to do some of the worst acting in their careers. The party scene and high scene are almost unbearable acting. I’ve read some of the treatise and dissertation defenses about how this is the point but c’mon…”it’s a dream!”, “it’s Brechtian alienation effect”, “it’s a commentary on society.” Or, it’s just poorly acted at times under the direction of a drill sergeant who is micromanaging these very particular Hollywood stars who don’t know how to work with him. I love Kidman and I’m in no way a Cruise hater but yeesh. Cruise definitely gets better in the latter half when he has something to do besides walk around half mast looking for people to take to bone town. And Kidman pretty much disappears from the film. The colors are beautiful. Love what Kubrick and team did with the palette. Some cool locations and camerawork too. Was Kubrick killed by the cabal for this film? Honestly, I don’t think they really cared because this film’s reception for the layman was, “Kidman is naked a bunch. Let’s goooo!” rather than some Epstein-like conspiracy reveal. But it is a fun conspiracy theory to engage with. Someday, someone will sit me down and explain why this is a masterpiece. Until then, in my opinion, it is a gigantic whiff. But I look forward to the future education by EWS lovers! I did think this got so much better in the second half. 80 mins in it was in my worst films of all time list and a 1/2 ⭐️ I found this fascinating quote in an old article from The Guardian: “Stanley called me about two weeks before he died," (R. Lee) Ermey told Radar Online. "We had a long conversation about Eyes Wide Shut. He told me it was a piece of shit and that he was disgusted with it and that the critics were going to have him for lunch. He said Cruise and Kidman had their way with him - exactly the words he used." Kudos for his big swing and understanding of what a shit show this was.

We rarely suffer any physical harm from “betrayal.” Betrayal is something that is born in the heart, something that wounds the heart. And it’s incredibly difficult to grasp what betrayal actually is. Perhaps betrayal only comes into existence when either you or the other person feels that something is “betrayal.” That’s how I think it works. Betrayal can exist even without any action behind it, and in essence, it is just as much a betrayal as one that involves an actual act. If both are guilty, then perhaps neither is. Surely, everyone lives with countless betrayals inside themselves that they never actually act upon. And perhaps that is why, when we ourselves are betrayed, we suffer from the fact that we have no choice but to forgive the other person as someone who is guilty of the very same thing we are. And because it hurts, we close our eyes to it. Both of us. The movie does feel somewhat drawn-out overall, but I found it interesting how it makes you feel that everything that happens between people ultimately happens inside their hearts. Perhaps I felt that even more strongly because the two leads, who are both beautiful yet somehow strangely devoid of sex appeal, seemed almost like empty “vessels.”

Mesmo assim quis dar uma chance pra esse pq né, Tom Cruise, Nicole Kidman e todo mundo fala super bem. E assim, o filme n é ruim, mas senti a mesma coisa q senti vendo Laranja Mecânica: eu simplesmente n me importo com quase nada q acontece. Os personagens, as tramas, tudo passa por mim e n me envolve muito. Talvez eu só n entenda a “mente do Kubrick” e todos os significados profundos e blablabla ou talvez eu só n tenha gostado mesmo, e tipo, eu entendi oque ele quis passar aqui de “ah o outro lado da Elite, a parte que você nunca viu etc”, achei muito interessante os figurinos e cenários, me lembrou o clássico Baile Surrealista dos Rothschild (1972), massss….. Pra mim o filme começa ok, a discussão entre Alice e Bill é interessante, mas ele realmente começa a subir quando o Bill encontra o pianista, consegue a senha e começa a se meter numa coisa q ele claramente n faz ideia da dimensão. A sequência da mansão é facilmente o ápice do filme. A trilha bizarra, aquelas máscaras, aquelas pessoas, aquele clima completamente estranho, ali eu tava realmente  bom. Dá aquela sensação de q ele é uma formiguinha no meio de algo gigantesco e q se descobrirem quem ele é meio q fudeu. Depois ainda tem aquela conversa com a Alice sobre o sonho dela, q abre espaço pra um monte de teoria sobre ela ter alguma ligação com aquilo, ter passado por algo parecido, memória apagada slaaaa. Só q depois disso o filme vira uma grande água de salsicha. É basicamente o Bill indo atrás de pistas e descobrindo coisas q a gente meio q já imaginava, gente ligada à seita morreu, desapareceu ou provavelmente se fudeu. E fica nisso por tempo demais. E aquele final? Depois de tudo aquilo, achei tão ruimzinho e sem graça q só me deixou puto. + o filme deveria se chamar “Tom Cruise e sua pika de mel”

RATING: Below Average (4/10) My initial takeaway is that I’m heavily concerned this is one of my brother’s favorite movies. For context, whether it makes me prude or conservative, I’m not a massive fan of extensive nudity in films. I prefer to keep my box office and boobs separate. I also couldn’t appreciate the messaging from Kubrick due to the constant sexual undertones and overall “cuck energy”. The film also lacks a cohesive plot and rather aimlessly follows Cruise’s character, really only displaying his prowess and range as an actor. His performance makes me wish a top tier director would cast him for a film outside his current action blockbusters. Sydney Pollack felt flat and lackluster while Nicole Kidman was exploited and one dimensional in an unremarkable supporting cast. On a high note, the cult mansion scene was executed perfectly, finding myself heavily invested in the intoxicating atmosphere. This act highlighted the simple, jarring score, setting a precedent for building suspense. I did feel satisfied with the ending as in a convoluted way, it tied the lack of plot together. While I’d never watch it again, I could see the appeal to a certain audience as it emulates a Walmart-version Midsommar.

Eyes Wide Shut was a mixed experience for me, I didn't particularly love the movie itself, but it was undoubtedly an unsettling and terrifying watch. Cruise and Kidman deliver strong performances, yet the slow pacing makes it a tough ride at times.What stays with you, however, is the atmosphere and the deeply disturbing questions it raises. It forces you to look at power, secrecy, and the shadowy worlds of the elite, leaving you questioning what truly happens behind closed doors and how little we actually know about the world around us.Even if it wasn't my favorite watch, it remains a fascinating, eerie experience that leaves a lasting impression. A unique film, but definitely not for everyone

So this ones for all those sophisticated gooners I see. I had always heard that this film was out there and that the fact that Kubrick died before the editing stage really shows cause god damn is this movie way longer than. it needs to be. I think they had an interesting enough story with this but a lot of it's steam was lost in the editing room with unnecessary long shots, reveals that could easily be figured out by the audience that is instead thrown at your face, it all seemed really dull. The story always seemed to be going somewhere, and then landing flat on its face, almost like the person with all of the ideas died and what were left with is someones interpretation of what they actually wanted. So many underlying themes that go nowhere, messaging that I thought was going to be about the strain of marriage and love that ended up being nothing more than just talking about sex. I don't know, it's lighting and mood are fantastic, but the rest is a complete mess that only one of the greats could've untangled.
